Header:
Date: 2026-12-15
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Varga (Redwood Product), Lena Ortiz (Cobalt ML Lead), Tom Nguyen (Cobalt SRE), Priya Rao (Cobalt CTO)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quick Optimize walk: INT8 vs FP8 profiles. Raj ran through latency numbers and quality delta on Cobalt-like QA tasks. Talked about caching, batching and fallback to hosted model variants. Agreed to benchmark and share docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Today Raj will run through Optimize quantization profiles - INT8 and FP8 - and we'll cover quality vs latency tradeoffs.
[00:10] Lena: Hi! Thanks, excited. We sent over the sample QA set, right? That should give you a sense of our tail latency SLOs.
[00:18] Raj: Yep we got the set, have a look - we ran a quick pass locally. A couple of caveats up front: FP8 gives you near-fp16 quality on most of the QA prompts, INT8 saves more on tokens but sometimes drops a percent or two on exact-match.
[00:34] Tom: How big is that quality drop? like top-1 accuracy or F1?
[00:38] Raj: For the demo dataset we saw around 1.2-2.8% hit on exact-match on long context QAs for INT8, FP8 was typically <0.5% delta. But latency improvements were material: INT8 reduced per-token latency by ~18-25% versus FP16 baseline; FP8 sat around 10-14% improvement.
[01:05] Priya: That aligns with what we worried about - our SLAs are pretty tight, P95 under 300ms. If INT8 helps get us below that but costs a bit on quality, could we selectively use INT8 only for non-critical prompts?
[01:18] Raj: Absolutely, that's the common pattern. You can route by policy in Redwood Optimize: critical routes pinned to FP8 or FP16, lower-priority to INT8. Also prefix caching helps for repeated prompts, so you may not need INT8 as much if caching hits are high.
[01:31] Lena: How does this interact with KV cache and long-context performance? We have a lot of multi-turn dialogs.
[01:36] Raj: KV cache behaves the same; quant profiles affect compute for new tokens. For multi-turn, you'll see the biggest benefit on generation-heavy flows. For retrieval-augmented use cases where the prefix grows, FP8 keeps quality while still saving compute. INT8 can be tuned with per-layer calibration to avoid severe regressions on long contexts.
[01:54] Tom: Any hardware constraints? we're running on G5 and A10p in our infra.
[01:58] Raj: Redwood's runtime picks kernels per hardware. On A10p we saw slightly better INT8 throughput relative to fp16, G5 similarly benefits; FP8 is a bit newer and gives consistent wins on the newer Ampere-class and Hopper variants. We'll surface those model/hardware profiles in the Optimize UI and in the profile recommendations.
[02:18] Maya: Quick note, we have a public profile library in the Console under Optimize -> Quant Profiles; Raj can show a live demo.
[02:24] Raj: Cool, I'll share my screen - give me one sec.
[02:35] [screen-share starts]
[02:40] Raj: This is the Optimize console. Top-left you can pick a model and a workload. For Cobalt's QA workload we recommended two candidate profiles: profile-a (FP8-balanced) and profile-b (INT8-aggressive). You can see the estimated token-cost delta and latency delta here, those are from our internal benchmarking harness.
[03:05] Lena: The latency column - are those real numbers or estimates?
[03:09] Raj: They're estimates based on the model and GPU family and your reported batch sizes. We recommend running a short POC benchmark with your actual traffic pattern to confirm. That's part of the next steps.
[03:20] Tom: Is there an automated rollback if quality regresses?
[03:22] Raj: Yes - rollout policies support canary, A/B split, and automatic rollback if the quality monitors (we tie to your eval set and behavioral checks) drop beyond thresholds. You can configure thresholds per route.
[03:35] Priya: About security - we have requirements for KMS and audit logs. Does Optimize integrate with our KMS?
[03:41] Raj: Yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and all inference traces are logged to audit streams. For hosted, we support encrypted at-rest keys and we can enable dedicated audit retention for enterprise. We'll send the SOC2 / ISO docs - and Elena will follow up with the security pack.
[04:00] Elena: I'll drop those in the thread after the call. Also note there's an option to run the Dedicated pool under your VPC for extra isolation.
[04:08] Lena: Great. For the benchmark, could you run comparisons across: FP16 baseline, FP8-balanced, INT8-calibrated, and also an INT8 with per-layer exceptions?
[04:18] Raj: Yep that's exactly what we planned. We'll do FP16, FP8, INT8-calibrated, and INT8 with selective layers kept in FP16. We'll collect quality metrics (exact-match, EM at different answer lengths), latency distribution (P50/P95/P99), and cost-per-1000 tokens.
[04:35] Maya: I'll also include a sample pricing scenario so you can see committed vs pay-as-you-go numbers.
[04:40] Priya: On cost - what's the rough delta between FP8 and INT8 in terms of $/1M tokens? ballpark is fine.
[04:46] Raj: Ballpark: FP8 typically reduces compute cost ~20-30% vs FP16; INT8 can be 35-50% lower depending on kernels and batch efficiency. But remember quantization tuning can affect recurrence and sometimes requires more tokens for reruns if quality drops, so net cost depends on your failure/retry rate.
[05:05] Tom: Any pitfalls to watch out for during calibration?
[05:08] Raj: Calibration set representativeness is key. Also avoid calibrating on only short prompts if you have long-context flows. Watch out for outliers - a small set of adversarial prompts can skew per-layer scaling. We provide a calibration tool in the repo I'll share.
[05:25] Lena: Can you show the quality vs latency graph for our dataset?
[05:28] Raj: Sure pulling it now... [short pause] okay here's the graph - x-axis is latency delta relative to FP16, y-axis is EM delta. You can see FP8 clusters near the origin, INT8 shifts right with a tail of worse EM on the longest queries.
[05:48] Priya: That tail concerns us - our SLAs prefer predictable latency, not only median. What's the P99 impact on INT8?
[05:54] Raj: P99 increases modestly when batch sizes are small, because INT8 kernels sometimes have different kernel launch behavior; however in our continuous batching runtime we've optimized that. For your traffic patterns (small-batch, low-latency), FP8 may be the safer choice initially.
[06:12] Maya: Quick interjection - many customers start on FP8 for canary and then evaluate moving some non-critical routes to INT8 after a week of metrics look good.
[06:21] Lena: Ok that process seems sensible. What's the expected time to run the 48-hour benchmark? like how soon can you start?
[06:28] Raj: If you provide the 10k QA pairs and a small traffic simulator, we can start within 24 hours and provide initial results in 48 hours. Full analysis with configs and recommended rollout plan within 72 hours.
[06:40] Tom: Any additional infra we need to enable? network egress or firewall rules for Private?
[06:45] Raj: For hosted no special firewall rules, just API access and an S3 bucket with the dataset. For Dedicated or Private we might need VPC peering or a private link - we'll coordinate with your infra team.
[06:58] Priya: Pricing - are there commit tiers for Dedicated that factor into the cost calculus for FP8 vs INT8?
[07:04] Maya: Yes, Dedicated reserved capacity discounts change unit economics. We can model both pay-as-you-go and committed pricing so you can see break-even points.
[07:12] Lena: In our case we expect steady usage, so committed may make sense. We'll evaluate after seeing the benchmark cost numbers.
[07:19] Raj: One more note: the Optimize console also surfaces per-route token-level cost and expected latency given the profile - that makes it easy to compare scenarios without running full prod tests initially.
[07:30] Tom: Are there any known issues with hallucination rates when using INT8?
[07:33] Raj: It's not a direct correlation, but quality degradation can manifest as paraphrase changes or missing tokens which in QA equates to lower EM. Hallucination increases are typically small but we monitor by measuring factuality checks in the eval harness.
[07:48] Lena: Could we do a small canary for FP8 on 10% of traffic first?
[07:52] Raj: Yes, canary or A/B is supported and we can tie automatic rollback to EM threshold drops.
[07:58] [screen-share: config snippet appears]
[08:05] Raj: Here's a sample quantization config: profile name, per-layer exceptions, fallback policy, and the routing rule. You can see how to pin routes and set the monitor.
[08:20] Lena: That config example will be super helpful.
[08:22] Raj: I'll post it to the repo as well.
[08:27] Priya: Any compliance questions - data residency? our data must stay in EU for some clients.
[08:33] Elena: For data residency we have EU regions and you can deploy Dedicated in a region under a contract. Private on-prem is also an option if needed. We'll include that in the security doc pack.
[08:45] Maya: Ok we're hitting a lot of the checklist - can we recap next steps?
[08:49] Lena: Sure.
[08:50] Maya: Raj will run the 48-hour benchmark across FP16/FP8/INT8 and INT8 partial layers using the 10k dataset. Raj will upload the results and suggested profile to the shared Drive.
[08:59] Raj: Correct. I'll also include per-model/hardware notes and the config snippets.
[09:03] Maya: I'll send pricing scenarios for committed vs pay-as-you-go. Elena will send security and SOC2/ISO docs. Cobalt to share the 10k QA set and any latency SLO specifics.
[09:14] Priya: Timeline ok: we'll aim to provide dataset by end of day tomorrow.
[09:18] Lena: Yes we'll get it in.
[09:20] Maya: Great. Anything else?
[09:22] Tom: Quick question - if we do Dedicated, can we still use Optimize UI or is it different?
[09:27] Raj: You'll get the same Console experience; Dedicated just binds a dedicated pool and the routing rules apply the same.
[09:33] Lena: perfect. thanks everyone.
[09:36] Maya: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the emails and links.
[09:40] [meeting ends]
